guard_streams.source: Ofcom fines Virgin Media £28m for repeatedly preventing customers from cancelling contracts

facts.detail: Ofcom published the Virgin Media cancellation enforcement decision on 8 July 2026.
The investigation covered calls made between 1 January 2022 and 11 September 2024.
Virgin Media used a two-tier retention process in which only second-tier agents could process cancellations.
Ofcom found unnecessary transfers, repeated holds, deliberate call drops and failures to process cancellations.
Ofcom imposed a £28 million fine and required Virgin Media to check remedies for affected complainants.

guard_streams.source: Report: Complaints about broadband, landline, mobile and pay-TV services

facts.detail: Ofcom last updated the complaints report on 23 July 2026.
Provider complaint volumes are published quarterly relative to customer bases, as complaints per 100,000 customers.
Overall complaints decreased in Q1 2026 compared with Q4 2025.
TalkTalk was the most complained-about fixed-broadband provider in Q1 2026.
Plusnet and Sky generated the fewest fixed-broadband complaints.

facts.detail: Ofcom last updated the BT landline-only customer statement on 16 March 2026.
BT confirmed a £1 monthly line-rental increase from 31 March 2026 for a 12-month period, with no call-plan increase.
Landline-only customers use a BT phone line without broadband from BT or another provider.
Ofcom describes the shrinking customer group as largely older and less likely to switch provider.
BT offers an eligible landline-only social tariff priced at £10 per month.

guard_streams.source: Investigation into Virgin Media’s compliance with rules relating to vulnerable consumers and access to emergency organisations

facts.detail: Ofcom opened the Virgin Media telecare investigation on 12 December 2023.
Ofcom issued a Confirmation Decision on 1 December 2025.
Ofcom found a General Condition C5.2 contravention between August 2022 and December 2023.
The decision identified failures to record telecare status and unsafe disconnection practices.
Ofcom imposed a £23.8 million financial penalty.

facts.detail: BDUK published the Hubs Evaluation Plan on 15 August 2025.
The publication covers remaining evaluation activity planned between 2024 and 2027.
BDUK commissioned Belmana, Hatch and GC Insights to conduct the evaluation.
The intervention connects remote public buildings such as schools, GP surgeries and libraries to gigabit-capable broadband.
The initial intervention ran through Rural Gigabit Connectivity from 2019 to 2022, followed by GigaHubs under Project Gigabit.
